ICSSR invites original manuscripts for a Special Issue on "Understanding India's Demographic Shift: Trends, Transitions and Policy Perspectives"

  • Home

Indian Social Science Review (ISSR), a Multidisciplinary Journal of Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), invites original manuscripts for a Special Issue on "Understanding India's Demographic Shift: Trends, Transitions and Policy Perspectives".

India is home to over one-sixth of the world's population and represents one of the most dynamic, complex, and diverse demographic landscapes globally. As one of the world's most diverse societies, India has uniquely sustained its fundamental demographic rubric through centuries of historical transformations, including major waves of colonization, political transitions, economic restructuring, and rapid globalization, while simultaneously undergoing profound structural changes.

India is currently at a critical demographic juncture. While the country continues to benefit from its demographic dividend phase, it is also experiencing multiple demographic transitions, including regional variations in fertility, population ageing, migration and labour mobility, urbanization, changing family structures, and rapid digital transformation. While India's demographic dividend offers significant opportunities for economic growth, these changes also present important policy challenges requiring robust evidence-based research, policy planning, and governance. Addressing issues such as ageing, migration, human capital, climate-induced mobility, and regional demographic differences is essential for achieving inclusive development and realizing the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

To advance scholarly discourse in this important area, ICSSR invites high-quality, original manuscripts that offer innovative theoretical, empirical, methodological, comparative, or policy-oriented insights into India's demographic transformation. Contributions from scholars across the social sciences and allied disciplines including demography, sociology, anthropology, economics, geography, political science, public policy, public health, development studies, statistics, and related fields are especially encouraged.

Themes

Papers may address, but are not limited to, the following themes:

  • Population Dynamics and Demographic Transition
  • Demographic Data, Methods, Population Projections and Spatial Demography
  • Population Policy, Census, Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (CRVS)
  • Religion, Population Change and Social Transformation
  • Religious Conversion and Demographic Dynamics
  • Population Governance, Public Policy and Demographic Planning
  • Comparative and International Demography
  • Cross-Border Migration, Border Governance, National Security and Demographic Change
  • Janjatiya Populations and Social Diversity in Demography
  • Population, Environment and Climate Change
  • Population Ageing and the Longevity Transition
  • Fertility, Family Formation, Marriage and Reproductive Behaviour
  • Structure and Dynamics of Kinship Demography
  • Migration, Mobility, Urbanization and Spatial Dynamics
  • Population, Employment and Labour Market Transformation
  • Demography, Human Capital and Inclusive Development
  • Gender, Population and Social Inequality
  • Health, Nutrition and Population
  • Digital Society, Artificial Intelligence and Demographic Data Systems

IMPORTANT DATE

Submission Opens:26th August 2026
Last Date of Submission:21st November 2026| 06:00 PM

All manuscripts must be submitted online through the prescribed submission portal. Only manuscripts submitted through the online mode will be considered for review.

Authors are advised not to send their manuscripts directly to ICSSR by email or post. Manuscripts received directly by ICSSR will not be considered for review.
